report_name: Leaked AWS Keys with Admin Access Found Active by Truffle Security

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The investigation identified 768 active AWS keys, including 526 root keys and 242 IAM user keys with AdministratorAccess, which constitute valid cloud accounts that can be abused for unauthorized access.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: Thousands of AWS access keys were discovered publicly leaked in files within code repositories, datasets on Hugging Face, and CI/CD logs, where they were inadvertently committed by developers.

vulnerabilities.name: Publicly Exposed Cloud Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: A large-scale security issue where thousands of active Amazon Web Services (AWS) access keys, including hundreds with full administrative and root privileges, have been publicly exposed in code repositories and datasets for extended periods, creating a high risk of account takeover.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services
identities.description: Cloud service provider whose access keys were found leaked and active in public sources, posing a security risk to its customers.

identities.name: Hugging Face
identities.description: An AI platform identified as a major source of publicly leaked AWS keys found within user-contributed datasets and projects.

indicators.name: AWS Access Key ID Pattern
indicators.pattern:
title: AWS Access Key ID Pattern
id: 7e8b1c2a-9d3f-4e5a-b6c7-d8e9f0a1b2c3
status: experimental
description: Detects a string pattern matching the AWS Access Key ID format in files or logs, indicating a potential secret leak.
references:
  - https://gbhackers.com/768-leaked-aws-keys-still-active-with-full-admin/amp/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-23
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|re: 'AKIA[A-Z0-9]{16}'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the standard prefix for an AWS Access Key ID (`AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`) in command lines, which could indicate hardcoded credentials.

indicators.name: Exposed AWS Credentials File
indicators.pattern:
title: Exposed AWS Credentials File
id: f4a5b6c7-d8e9-4f0a-b1c2-d3e4f5a6b7c8
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of the default AWS credentials file, which may indicate a secret leak if found in an insecure location like a public repository.
references:
  - https://gbhackers.com/768-leaked-aws-keys-still-active-with-full-admin/amp/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-23
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.aws\credentials'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation or presence of the default AWS credentials file (`~/.aws/credentials`), which is a critical finding if discovered in a public code repository.
